title: The Normalised Wigner Negativity Rate as a Second-Moment Probe of Infall in AdS$_3$
abstract: In spread complexity, the average position of an operator along its Krylov chain, recovers the right radial momentum of an infalling particle in AdS, yet it is a measure of the first moment, irrespective of the spread of the wavepacket away from its classical trajectory. The rate of a normalized Krylov-Wigner negativity can be proposed as a diagnostic of the second moment of the boundary state that captures this spreading. Starting with the \emph{seed-normalized} Krylov-Wigner distribution -- that is, the Wigner transform of the descendant cloud, with the decaying return amplitude divided out -- we obtain an analytic Bessel form in the macroscopic limit and compute its total negativity explicitly. Retaining the Bessel variable all the way through, we find that the negativity goes as $\sinh^{4Δ}(πt/β)$, while the raw, seed-normalized state negativity saturates, as dictated by the $O(\sqrt{D})$ bound. Using the exact negative binomial statistics of the Krylov chain and the momentum dictionary of Caputa et al.~\cite{Caputa:2024}, the rate of the negativity scales as the growth rate of the Krylov variance at late time asymptotics \emph{if and only if} $Δ=1$, the Breitenlohner-Freedman saturating dimension in $AdS_3$. This dimensionality is special in that the negativity rate is the product of the proper radial position and momentum, $\mathcal{R} \propto \mathcal{C} P_ρ$, i.e., the rate of the tidal stretch of nearby geodesic falling into the horizon. We comment on the direction for future research, in particular the interpretation of the transverse string size operator in terms of the Krylov number operator through the common $SU(1,1)$ discrete series.
summary: This theoretical paper proposes using the rate of normalized Krylov-Wigner negativity as a sophisticated probe to measure wavepacket spreading in holographic CFT models dual to AdS$_3$. By linking this second-moment observable to the growth rate of the Krylov variance, the authors identify a special condition ($\Delta=1$) where the rate directly measures the tidal stretching experienced by infalling geodesics.
main_problem: The research aims to develop a diagnostic tool, based on the rate of normalized Krylov-Wigner negativity, that probes the second moment (spreading) of quantum wavepackets during time evolution in holographic CFT setups.
main_result: The negative rate scales with the growth rate of the Krylov variance if and only if the system dimension $\Delta=1$, which corresponds to the special Breitenlohner-Freedman saturation dimension in AdS$_3$.
method: The analysis combines techniques from quantum information (Wigner negativity), random matrix theory (Krylov chain/Lanczos algorithm), and holographic duality (AdS geometry).
model_or_system: The system models the time evolution of a local operator quench in a 2D CFT, dual to an infalling particle dynamics in AdS$_3$. The dynamics are analyzed via the Krylov Hamiltonian structure realizing $\mathfrak{su}(1, 1)$ algebra.
key_observables: Normalized Krylov-Wigner Negativity Rate, Spread Complexity (first moment), Krylov Variance, and the Bessel function form of the distribution.
important_parameters: The dimension $\Delta$ (related to the Breitenlohner-Freedman dimension) and the time scale $t/ eta$.
main_assumptions: A key conjecture relates the string-size operator ($\hat{N}_{	ext{str}}$) to the boundary Krylov number operator ($\hat{N}_{	ext{Krylov}}$), which is stated as a heuristic, not a proof.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes; the analysis relies on deriving closed forms for distributions (Negative Binomial) and asymptotic scaling laws involving $\sinh^4\Delta$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining first-moment probes (Spread Complexity) to introducing the second-moment probe (Negativity Rate). It establishes the mathematical framework using $\mathfrak{su}(1, 1)$ algebra and then connects this formalism to physical observables in AdS$_3$ via matching conditions derived from string theory fluctuations.
why_interesting: The connection between quantum information measures (negativity) and geometric properties (tidal stretching rate) provides a powerful, non-standard diagnostic tool for understanding the emergence of classical spacetime from quantum field theory dynamics.
